newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson Multimedia has $556 million loss - paper.
newsitem.headline: Thomson Multimedia has $556 million loss - paper.

text.p: Thomson Multimedia (TMM), the consumer electronics unit of state-owned Thomson SA, is set to report a net attributable loss of 3.0 billion francs ($556 million) for 1996, the Les Echos newspaper said on Thursday.
This would compare with a 1995 loss of 1.09 billion francs.
The group, slated for privatisation despite an aborted selloff late last year, is also expected to report an operating loss of 500 million francs against a profit of 352 million in 1995.
TMM posted a 3.0 billion franc net loss and 1.2 billion operating loss in the first half of the year, indicating it made some improvement in the second half.

Industry Minister Franck Borotra said on Wednesday that TMM would get a capital injection in the next few weeks. This recapitalisation, seen at 10 billion francs, will cut financing costs by 600 million francs.

In early December, the French government suspended a privatisation plan for Thomson under which conglomerate Lagardere Groupe would have bought the firm after a recapitalisation for one symbolic franc.

Lagardere would have merged the Thomson-CSF unit with its Matra Defence Espace unit and sold TMM to Daewoo Electronics of South Korea. Daewoo was angered by the government's decision not to go through with the sale.

TMM expects to be structurally profitable in 1998 when it will receive payments on patents of its GE/RCA U.S. unit under the terms of its orginial acquisition deal with General Electric Corp. ($1=5.395 French Franc)
